paragraphs.source_en:
It would appear that in transcribing this from Ashley, which has a mark that might be read as a comma
at the end of the first line but no other punctuation, Mary substituted ‘To’ for In as the first word of the
fourth line because she understood the adverbial force of that line to relate to come in the third line. But
in transcribing Mary Copybk 2, she added commas at the end of lines 2 and 3 and retained In (which is
also the reading of the draft in Nbk 10 f. 14r) in line four, making line 3 parenthetical, and having line 4
qualify spread at the end of line 2, an arrangement that she reproduced in 1839.
